extracted_by: hand, T-0292 — the Democrat read, October 1834; c006-c009 by hand, T-0997 — the town meeting against gambling of 24 October 1834
note: Vol. I No. 48. The town is on page 3. This issue completes the fire ordinance begun on 1834-10-01 — the trustees met at the Tremont House on 13 October and gave the wardens command at a fire, in force from 25 October — and it carries no Chicago letter list, only the Hennepin and Plainfield ones, which are recorded and not minted. THE TOWN IS ALSO ON PAGE 2, columns 1 and 2, which T-0292 did not read: a town meeting for the suppression of gambling, J. H. Kinzie in the chair and Hans Crocker secretary, which appointed a committee of 70. T-0997 extracted it as c006-c009. The segmenter's column-2 crop sets physical column 1 in its left margin and physical column 2 after it, so each of those claims cuts ONE physical column out with `locator.spans`; column 1's own block is a SECOND, offset strip of the same text and the two cannot be aligned, which is why the roll's head is declared unreadable rather than guessed.

claims.notes: THE ROLL OF THE COMMITTEE APPOINTED AGAINST GAMBLING, and the largest single list of townspeople acting on a stated evening that this corpus holds. The interleaving IS resolved here and the resolution is mechanical, not a judgement: the segmenter's column-2 crop sets physical column 1 in a 14-to-21-character left margin and physical column 2 after it, so `spans` cuts the column out character by character and the quote is column 2 and nothing else. Lines 968 and 977 carry no left margin and are quoted whole. WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED, and is declared rather than guessed: the roll's HEAD is not on this page-2 crop at all — column 1's own block (lines 865-964) is a second, offset strip of the same physical column and its names do not line up with these, so how many of the seventy were printed and in what order cannot be recovered from the transcription. No page image is deposited for this issue (corpus.json carries the .docx and its .txt only), so there is nothing to arbitrate with. TWENTY-ONE name positions are legible here; eight of them cannot give a forename and carry [?] in the position the initial was printed (T-0397); two surnames — `A. N. Ful[…]` and `M. M'Cle[…]` — are cut by the column edge mid-word and are NOT completed. A. N. Fullerton and Alexander Fullerton are both already in this gazetteer and the initials fit, but `[…]` is this corpus's mark of ABSENCE and not a licence to supply: the letters were never printed on the crop, so there is nothing here for a bracket to stand in. The same refusal is applied to `H. G. Hub[…]` in c008, where a printed word-break hyphen shows the compositor continuing a word the margin then cut away. `WW. Sherwan` is read `W. Sherman` on the rn/m confusion the Tesseract fallback makes throughout this column; the doubled W is the column rule. This column is the Tesseract fallback by the transcription's own statement at line 967, so weight every reading here below a Vision column of the same issue. A NAME THE COLUMN EDGE CUT IN HALF IS A POSITION, NOT A PERSON, AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE. `A. N. Ful[…]`, `M. M'Cle[…]`, `H. G. Hub[…]`, `[?] Hau[…]` and `Hon. R. J. […]` each stand in `normalized` at the place they were printed, with `[…]`, this corpus's mark of absence, where the crop stops — and NONE of them is given an entity. An entity asserts that a named person is here, and half a surname cannot name one. The refusal is not only editorial: `tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py` splits a name into surname and forename with the brackets stripped, so `H. G. Hub[…]` reaches `tools/mint_civic_residents.py` as the plain name `H G Hub`, its bracketed-as-uncertain refusal cannot fire on it, and the town gains a card headed `The Hub household`. Five of those were minted here before this claim was narrowed and they were deleted. The guard's blind spot is real and is filed separately; this claim does not walk into it. `}. Ven De Bogart` is read `H. Ven De Bogart`: the damaged glyph is a reading of a letter the page DOES set, not a supply of one it omits, and this gazetteer already carries an H. Van Den Bogart. Leaving the initial `[?]` would have been the worse record rather than the humbler one — the surname splitter downstream takes the first token as a forename, so `[?] Ven De Bogart` mints a man called Ven Debogart, who never existed. `J[no]. S. C. Hogan` is written `J. S. C. Hogan` for the same reason and because that is the form this corpus already prints him in seven times.

claims.notes: THE REPORT ITSELF — physical column 1, quoted from where its characters actually are, which is the LEFT MARGIN of the segmenter's column-2 crop. The locator says column 2 because that is the block these characters stand in and a locator must name where the text IS; the text is column 1's. Read end to end the margin is continuous prose, which is what proves the cut: the meeting is organised, a committee of five is appointed by the chair to ascertain the extent to which gambling is carried on and who is engaged in it, and it reports to a meeting held Saturday the 25th. Then the Chair names a committee — H. G. Hubbard, Jno. S. C. Hogan, W. H. Kennicott, Grant Goodrich and one more whose surname the margin cuts at `Haux`, which is FIVE and matches `sisting of five` two lines above — and four further names follow after the word `[f]ive`: Hon. R. J[?], V. Owen, E. Kinzie and G. Spring[s]. WHETHER THOSE FOUR ARE A SECOND BODY OR THE SAME ONE IS NOT DECIDABLE HERE and is not decided: line 1088 of this crop reads `committee of nine`, which would make five and four into nine, but the margin at that point has drifted out of register with column 1's own block and the two cannot be aligned line for line. Every forename the margin does not deliver carries [?] in its printed position, and every surname the margin CUT carries `[…]`, the mark of absence — `H. G. Hub[…]` is not completed to Hubbard although `Hub-` carries the compositor's own word-break hyphen and Henry G. Hubbard is already in this gazetteer, and `[?] Hau[…]` is left open. `Goodiich` IS read Goodrich, because there the whole surname is printed and only ordinary OCR damage stands between the two. The `Hon. R. J` line is NOT expanded to R. J. Hamilton though the initials and the honorific both fit him. `E. K[in]zie` keeps its supply and is the one exception here: both ends of that surname are printed — `E. K` closes line 989 and `zie` opens line 990 — so the bracket stands in for two letters the margin lost between two letters it kept, which is a different thing from a word that simply stops. The margin's second line, `1. Hauritox;`, is where a name stood and it is left UNREAD: it is a plausible R. J. Hamilton, which would agree with the `Hon. R. J` line fourteen lines below, and it is an equally plausible mangling of the `Haux` at line 986 — and a reading that can be talked into two different men is not a reading. It is quoted as the transcription sets it and carries no entity. `Will[ia]m Forsyth` in c009 keeps its brackets in `normalized` and drops them in the entity, and the line between it and the five above is where the letters ARE: both ends of that forename are printed and the bracket stands in for letters lost BETWEEN letters the page delivers. A word the crop simply stops in the middle of has no second end, and that is the whole of the difference. `E. K[in]zie` IS a name by that test and is STILL given no entity, for a reason that is not about the page: `tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py` rule M2 attaches an initial-only forename to the one full forename of that surname carrying the initial, and the one E. Kinzie this corpus holds is Ellen Marion Kinzie, named in an old-settler DEATH NOTICE Fergus printed in 1843. Asserting the entity mints a household headed by her whose press witness is an 1834 gambling committee, which is a claim about a real named woman that this page does not make — the town carries John H., James, R. A. and John S. Kinzie besides, so the initial does not isolate anyone. A refusal declared in `newspapers/identity.json#refused_merges` does NOT stop it: the consolidation reports declared refusals and applies only declared MERGES, so there is no instrument here to refuse with. The reading stands in `normalized` where it belongs and the tie goes to the ticket filed on this.

claims.notes: COLUMN 1'S OWN BLOCK — the second, offset strip of the same report, and the only place the committee is given its SIZE: line 951 sets `a commuttee of 70 he app`, which is `a committee of 70 be appointed`, and lines 952-954 give it its charge — on all occasions to take notice of and report to the proper authorities every infraction of the laws against gambling. Lines 874-879 carry a first signature pair, JNO. H. KINZIE and HANS CROCKER, under an earlier committee that names William Forsyth and Grant Goodrich. THIS STRIP CANNOT BE JOINED TO c006 OR c008. It is not the left half of the same physical lines — 953 `and repurt to the` and the margin's `ithorities, every in-` at line 1092 read as one sentence but sit fifteen lines out of register, and 877 and 976 both set `Saturday the 25th`, so the two blocks overlap in content rather than abutting. Line 967 says this issue's column 2 fell back to Tesseract; the damage here is of the same kind. So the roll's HEAD, at lines 960-964, is recorded as unresolvable per name and NOT minted: `R 1 Hassleme, Bk` is quoted as it stands and left unread, `Kingie` and `Habhard` are legible as Kinzie and Hubbard but both men are already named elsewhere in this report and a third appearance at an unknown position would be an invented person, `Card, ine:` and `Bryc, 23 Smil` are fragments of two or three surnames apiece with no initials. Three entities only are taken from this claim, all of them from lines the strip sets whole. THE SEVENTY WERE NOT ALL PRINTED LEGIBLY AND THIS IS THE REASON. `Grant` at line 875 is printed without a surname and is normalized `Grant [Goodrich]` — the one supply this claim makes, and it is made because that exact string is ALREADY this gazetteer's reading of the same man from the Democrat of 1835-05-20 c013, so the alternative is not a more cautious record but a second phantom standing beside the first.
